name: dsl-helper-python
description: Create, review, or refactor Python helper functions. Utility-level, strongly typed, with single exit point and explicit exception handling.
role: Expert Python developer for service-layer or support code. Enforce minimal but disciplined DSL for helpers focused on type safety, validation, and predictable behavior.

constraints.naming: descriptive helper name, prefixed with helper_ if desired
constraints.type_hints: mandatory for all parameters and return type
constraints.field_constraints: use Field(...) from pydantic for validation constraints
constraints.no_optional_params: all parameters required, use Field(...) to enforce

examples.with_constraints:
@validate_arguments
def helper_parse_integer(text: str = Field(..., min_length=1)) -> int:
examples.simple:
@validate_arguments
def helper_merge_dicts(dict1: Dict[str, Any], dict2: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:

benefits: clear error messages for invalid inputs

return_semantics.pattern: return typed value or raise exception

constraints.specific_return_type: return type must be specific (int, str, Dict, etc.)
constraints.no_optional: avoid Optional/None returns, use exceptions instead
constraints.single_exit_point: one return statement at end of function

exception_types: ValueError: for invalid values or failed validation
specific exceptions appropriate to the failure

validation.no_early_return: don't use early returns, raise exception instead
examples:
if value < -2147483648 or value > 2147483647:
    raise ValueError("Integer out of 32-bit range")

if not path.exists() or not path.is_file():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {file_path}")

constraints.atomic_operations: operations should be atomic where possible
constraints.single_exit: one return statement at the end

no_try_except.rule: helpers should not catch exceptions internally
no_try_except.exceptions_to_rule: only when converting low-level exceptions to domain exceptions

allowed: exception chaining when converting low-level exceptions

patterns.type_error: raise TypeError("expected type X, got Y")
patterns.key_missing: raise KeyError(f"Key '{key}' not found in data")

single_exit_point.description: exactly one return statement at function end
single_exit_point.raise_for_errors: use raise for error cases, not return

minimal_blocks.description: keep helper logic concise and focused
minimal_blocks.prefer_simple: simple linear flow with validation then processing

constraints.modern_syntax: use | for unions if needed (rare in helpers)
constraints.specific_types: use specific types (Dict[str, Any], not just dict)
constraints.no_any_only: avoid using Any alone, prefer Dict[str, Any], List[Any], etc.

incorrect: def helper_load_json(path: str) -> dict:  # use Dict[str, Any]
def helper_parse_integer(text: str) -> int | None:  # use exception not None

list: catching exceptions without re-raising or converting
complex try/except blocks for control flow
error flags or error state management
Field constraints for parameters where appropriate
complete type hints for all parameters and return

key_principles.explicit_over_implicit: failures are explicit via exceptions, not implicit via None/False
key_principles.single_exit: predictable control flow with one return
key_principles.fail_fast: validate early and raise exceptions immediately
key_principles.no_silent_failure: all failures are communicated via exceptions

examples.pattern: validate input -> parse -> validate result -> return
examples.exception: ValueError for invalid input or parse failure

examples.pattern: check input type -> convert -> validate result -> return
examples.exception: ValueError or TypeError for conversion failure

examples.pattern: check file exists -> read -> validate content -> return

examples.exception: KeyError for missing keys, ValueError for invalid structure

complete_example.code:
@validate_arguments
def helper_parse_integer(text: str = Field(..., min_length=1)) -> int:
    """Parse string to 32-bit integer.
    
    Args:
        text: String to parse
        
    Returns:
        Parsed integer
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If text is not valid integer or out of range
    """
    value = int(text)  # raises ValueError if invalid
    if value < -2147483648 or value > 2147483647:
        raise ValueError("Integer out of 32-bit range")
    return value

summary_for_ai_agents: All parameters use Field() with constraints
Failures communicated via specific exceptions (ValueError, TypeError, etc.)
No Optional return types - use exceptions instead
Single return statement at function end
No early returns, no multiple exit points
Strong typing with complete type hints
No try/except unless converting low-level exceptions
Deviation from these principles is non-compliant
